Robust, IV, quantile and panel models in table_regression()

Source: R/table_regression_robust.R
table_regression_robust.Rd

table_regression() reads the fits of estimatr::lm_robust() and estimatr::iv_robust(), the instrumental-variable and censored models of AER::ivreg() and AER::tobit(), the quantile regressions of quantreg::rq(), and the fixed-effects estimators of fixest (feols(), feglm(), fepois(), femlm(), fenegbin()). The estimatr and fixest fits carry the variance they were computed with, and the table reports it unchanged. quantreg::rq() has an estimator family of its own, chosen through vcov. Absorbed fixed effects render as a Fixed effects: block at the top of the fit statistics.

Usage

table_regression(
  models,
  vcov = "classical",
  cluster = NULL,
  show_fit_stats = NULL,
  ...  # the arguments of every class: see ?table_regression
)

This family has no argument of its own. The other arguments are documented in table_regression(); the values they take for these models are listed below.

Engines

ClassEngineAMEExponentiateBlocksvcov
lm_robustestimatr::lm_robust()yes--classical (the fit's own)
iv_robustestimatr::iv_robust()yes--classical (the fit's own)
ivregAER::ivreg()yes--classical
tobitAER::tobit()yes--classical, CR1
rqquantreg::rq()yes--classical (= nid), nid, iid, ker, rank, bootstrap
fixestfixest::feols(), fixest::feglm(), fixest::fepois(), fixest::femlm(), fixest::fenegbin()yes (no for a GLM with fixed effects)OR / IRR (link)-classical (the fit's own)

AME: whether the average-marginal-effects columns are available. Exponentiate: what exponentiate = TRUE gives. Blocks: the labeled blocks of rows the class adds below its coefficients. vcov: the values of vcov the class accepts. The same rows are returned by subset(table_regression_models(), family == "Robust, IV, quantile, panel").

The AME is refused for a fixest GLM with fixed effects (feglm(), fepois(), femlm(), fenegbin(), whatever the family): marginaleffects, which computes it, cannot take into account the uncertainty of the fixed effects. It is refused too for a feols() with fixed effects fitted with lean = TRUE, which marginaleffects cannot predict from (re-estimate it with lean = FALSE). Other feols() fits and a GLM without fixed effects have it. The AME of a factor in i() sits on the rows of its coefficients, against the reference i() gives them (ref =). A level of a factor in i(), or a numeric variable that i() enters as categories, with no coefficient row gets no AME, nor does a factor that i() enters only in an interaction.

What the table shows

Coefficient rows. One row per coefficient, with the standard errors the fit carries (estimatr, fixest) or those of the vcov requested (rq). The note names the estimator.

Fixed effects. fixest fits, and estimatr fits built with fixed_effects =, disclose their absorbed fixed effects as a Fixed effects: block at the top of the fit statistics: one Yes / No row per factor, blank for the models without the concept in a mixed table. Varying-slope-only factors (Origin[[x]]) absorb no intercept: they read No when another model absorbs that factor, and add no row otherwise. The block is on by default ("fixed_effects" in show_fit_stats).

Fit statistics. See Fit statistics below.

Values of the shared arguments

vcov, cluster

estimatr, fixest and ivreg: "classical" only, which for estimatr and fixest is the variance the fit carries. tobit: "classical" and "CR1", as for survreg. rq: its own estimator family. See Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals.

show_fit_stats

The defaults of each class, and the "fixed_effects", "within_r2" and "n_groups" tokens; see Fit statistics.

exponentiate

Odds or rate ratios for the GLM-family fixest fits, as the link says.

nested

See Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals.

Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals

estimatr and fixest. These fits carry the variance they were computed with, estimatr's se_type = and whatever fixest's own vcov interface produced, and spicy never overwrites it. A vcov request other than "classical" is refused; set the estimator through the fitting package instead: se_type = (with clusters =) for estimatr, vcov = at estimation or in summary() for fixest. The note carries fixest's own label of the estimator (clustered, Newey-West, Conley, ...), fixest's "IID" written as "Classical". With IID errors, fixest's default small-sample correction (fixest::ssc()) multiplies the standard errors of a feglm() fit by sqrt((n - 1) / (n - K)) over those of its glm() twin with the fixed effects as dummies (a feols() fit already matches lm()), and summary(fit, ssc = fixest::ssc(K.adj = FALSE)) gives the glm() values.

quantreg::rq. Its own estimator family, not the sandwich vocabulary:

  • "classical" resolves to the heteroskedasticity-robust "nid" sandwich (Hendricks-Koenker, Hall-Sheather bandwidth), quantreg's own large-sample default and the analog of Stata's vce(robust).

  • "iid": the Koenker-Bassett homoskedastic estimator, as Stata's vce(iid).

  • "ker": the Powell kernel sandwich.

  • "rank": rank-score inversion, which gives intervals only: the SE, t and p cells render as dashes, and the AME columns, which need a variance matrix, are refused.

  • "bootstrap": quantreg's native boot.rq (bsmethod = "xy"). With cluster =, the wild gradient cluster bootstrap of Hagemann (2017), the one cluster-robust route for rq. A weighted rq fit refuses it: the resamplers do not carry the weights.

cluster with any other rq estimator is refused.

AER::tobit. A tobit fit is a survreg model, and takes the same estimator: "CR1" from sandwich::vcovCL(), the CR0 sandwich scaled by \(G/(G-1)\), G the number of clusters. The other CR* tokens and HC* are refused. Under "CR1", a nested hierarchy is tested by the Wald chi-square of the added coefficients on the robust matrix.

Hierarchical comparison (nested = TRUE). A quantile hierarchy gets c("f_change", "p_change"), the Wald-type test quantreg::anova.rq() reports, under "nid" and "rank"; under "iid" and "ker" it is a Wald F of the added coefficients, and under "bootstrap" a Wald chi-square. A fixest hierarchy is compared by likelihood-ratio test; a fit estimated with a non-iid vcov gets a Wald F when its coefficient tests are t (feols, and feglm with a family whose dispersion is estimated) and a Wald chi-square when they are z (fepois, femlm, fenegbin, and feglm with the binomial or Poisson family). See Hierarchical (nested) model comparison in table_regression().

Fit statistics

lm_robust defaults to c("nobs", "r2", "adj_r2"), iv_robust to "nobs" alone, and an IV fixest::feols() shows neither R-squared nor AIC: the 2SLS R-squared is not the classical one. Asked for, it is the R-squared of ivreg(), on the structural residuals. The AIC and BIC of a fixest model are those of its lm(), glm() or MASS::glm.nb() twin with the fixed effects as dummies; see Vocabulary tokens in table_regression().

  • "fixed_effects": the Fixed effects: block, on by default.

  • "within_r2": the R-squared of the model with the fixed effects partialed out, a default for feols except an IV one, on request for estimatr. GLM-family fixest fits report fixest's McFadden pr2 instead.

  • "n_groups": one N (<factor>) row per absorbed factor, on request.

Named in the call, "fixed_effects", "within_r2" and "n_groups" are refused when no model of the table absorbs fixed effects, a fixest fit without | fe included. "within_r2" is refused too when no model of the table has a value for it (an IV feols(), a GLM-family fixest fit).

What is refused, and why

  • Every vcov other than "classical" for estimatr and fixest fits: the variance is chosen at fit time (see above).

  • For rq: HC*, since quantile regression has no working residuals or hat values ("nid" is the heteroskedasticity-robust estimator here, a sparsity-based quantile sandwich, not an HC variant); CR*, since there is no cluster-robust sandwich for it (use "bootstrap" with cluster =); and "jackknife", whose leave-one-out form is inconsistent for quantiles: the quantile objective is not differentiable, so dropping one observation can move the fit discontinuously.

  • nested = TRUE across two fixest fits that absorbed different fixed effects. fixest counts every absorbed level as an estimated parameter, so a test across two | fe structures measures the change in the absorbed effects together with the change in the coefficients, and the two cannot be separated. Hold the | fe part fixed across the hierarchy.

  • The AME of a fixest GLM with fixed effects, and of a feols() with fixed effects fitted with lean = TRUE (see Engines).

  • A fixest fit with fixed effects only: it has no coefficient row to show.

References

Hagemann, A. (2017). Cluster-robust bootstrap inference in quantile regression models. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 112(517), 446-456. doi:10.1080/01621459.2016.1148610

See also

table_regression() for the arguments shared by all classes; table_regression_models() for the registry of supported classes and the other families; the Publication-ready regression tables article.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("quantreg", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- quantreg::rq(wellbeing_score ~ age + sex, tau = 0.5,
                      data = sochealth)
  print(table_regression(fit))

  # The homoskedastic estimator instead of the default "nid".
  print(table_regression(fit, vcov = "iid"))
}
